title: Tooling: 1.88× faster production joint-dual replay via containment masks with identical receipts
body:
## Change and scope

At base `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, `scripts/experiments/binary_frame_replay.py:replay` still paid an O(outputs × triples) literal scan for each paid output when checking expected source symbols. Aaron Wang’s opt-in adapter `research/joint-dual-replay-fast/` (incorporated [#1880](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1880)) already proved exact containment masks with identical receipts. This PR wires that equivalent check into the **production** source used by `make joint-dual-verify`.

Only the source pin for `scripts/experiments/binary_frame_replay.py` changes inside `certificates/joint-dual-kappa.json`, `certificates/skip-frame-kappa.json`, and `research/joint-dual/SOURCE.json` (plus the consequent `source_manifest_sha256` / skip-frame certificate digest). Compiler replay bytes and every assertion / check_word / full-basis orientation receipt stay identical.

**Tooling improvement; no new kappa.** Selected frontier untouched.

## Result

On Linux / CPython 3.12.3 (Linux-6.12.94+-x86_64-with-glibc2.39), five alternating fresh-process pairs timing both pinned words gave median wall time **5.873 → 3.120 seconds (1.88×)**. Timing is host-descriptive and is not a correctness gate. Every replay receipt matches the baseline checker fieldwise. The measured path is both-words `replay()` (the historical checker used by `make joint-dual-verify`), not full make wall time including C++/transitions/unittest.

Package: `research/joint-dual-replay-production/`.
Tip: `8fdb992c7d40239f8a5b7602fa6f4636f3d97961`.

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 -I -B research/joint-dual-replay-production/verify.py
python3.12 -I -O -B research/joint-dual-replay-production/verify.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/joint-dual-replay-production
python3.12 -I -B research/joint-dual-replay-production/benchmark.py --rounds 5
```

Expected:

```text
PASS_JOINT_DUAL_REPLAY_PRODUCTION words=[23, 25] outputs=12261 receipts=2 no_new_kappa
PASS_JOINT_DUAL_REPLAY_PRODUCTION_O_POLICY refused_by_assert_gate=2 no_new_kappa
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/joint-dual-replay-production outcome=completed
PASS_IDENTICAL_JOINT_DUAL_REPLAY_PRODUCTION_RECEIPTS
```

Default verify is read-only. Historical checks use `assert` and deliberately refuse to load under `-O` (same production policy as before). Full `make verify`, selected cold replay, Lean, and multiplication-theorem obligations were not rerun for this isolated historical-checker change.

## Overlap and credit

Closest priors (different delivery): Aaron Wang’s `research/joint-dual-replay-fast/` / [#1880](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1880) (opt-in containment masks; this is the production wiring), [CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#756](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/756), [CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#2194](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2194) / [#2210](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2210) / [#2231](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2231) (same production-promotion pattern on other objects). No competing open PR on production `binary_frame_replay.replay` at refresh.

Chafik Boukhalfa authored the joint-dual / binary-frame replay verifier path. Aaron Wang authored the containment-mask algorithm. Prepared by Wentao Li ([VictorLiwentao](https://github.com/VictorLiwentao), [@Is__Victor](https://x.com/Is__Victor)) with substantial AI assistance, under Apache-2.0.
